question: Does the architecture cleanup introduce material CPU runtime regressions on fixed workloads?

measurement.state_stream: random.Random(120); 1000 sequential states; legal action at index modulo legal-action count
measurement.search: 10 fixed starting states, 32 iterations each; fresh roots; default SearchConfig
measurement.inference: 20 batches of 64 states; maximum inference batch size 64
measurement.optimization: 20 Adam updates of 64 positions, learning rate 0.001; weights retained between repetitions

after_api_adaptations: Use engine/game, learning model/inference/batch/train/loss modules, and search/mcts imports.
Pass np.random.default_rng(i) to run_mcts; keep original process reseeding calls in measured adapter.
reproduction.runner_note: Same fixed work; omits now-unused process-global reseeding in search. Measured results above use the API-only adapter, not a later runner invocation.

limitations: Same local host and Python environment, measured sequentially rather than in randomized alternating runs.
Only three timed samples per workload; no confidence interval or cross-environment claim.
State-generation algorithm and search budgets match, but owned search RNG changes traversal trajectories.
Transition speedup coincides with removal of automatic deep invariant validation; explicit validation remains available and tested.
Small inference and optimizer timing differences are not attributed to an implementation improvement.
No training convergence, playing strength, GPU/MPS, or multiprocessing throughput was measured.
After measurement preceded the review commits; per-file digests match the measured_source_commit for all listed source files.

suite_validation.test_change: Retired interface/compatibility assertions were removed or replaced; behavioral tests cover new model-free layers, safe tree reuse, owned RNG, replay, continuation, and real workflows.
